description:
`enum_predicate_search` still has no detector for the pull-layer work that made
this tiny fixture take seconds to compile. The old stopwatch was correctly
retired: `timeout.run_secs` and `timeout.interp_secs` remain 20-second hang
backstops and must not become performance assertions again.

## Current evidence

At origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`, three separate production
runs of:

    fz2 --log-telemetry <tmp>.jsonl interp \
      fixtures2/behavior/enum_predicate_search.fz

completed successfully with identical stdout and identical work totals:

- 2,299 `pull.product.settled` events whose product kind is
  `callable_construction`
- 6,417 product settlements in total
- 1,441 `work_graph.applied` completions
- 6,378 demand-cone derivations

The emitted backend inventory is now 206 executables, pinned by
`backend_inventory_width_stays_pinned_on_the_target_fixtures`.

The ticket's former 2,625-settlement / 242-executable measurement is therefore
stale and must not be installed.

## Why existing ratchets do not close this gap

The public-trace suite now pins this fixture at 538 `AnalyzeActivation`
evaluations and 1,349 total formula evaluations, and verifies that every
evaluation names moved evidence. Those are valuable scheduler-work ratchets,
but they do not bound this defect's dimension: a product settled during a pull
is not a job. A stable increase in callable-construction product settlements
can leave the formula count unchanged.

`CausalReport` already derives per-product settlement counts from the same
public JSONL stream written by `fz2 --log-telemetry`; no new compiler counter is
needed.

## Goal

Give `enum_predicate_search` a machine-independent maximum of 2,299
callable-construction product settlements, declared in the fixture's
frontmatter and enforced from production public telemetry.

## Build

- Extend unified fixture metadata with an explicit maximum-metric form, for
  example:

      assert.max_metric.pull.callable_construction.settlements: 2299

  Maximum semantics are required: fail only when actual work exceeds the
  declared value. An improvement may pass and should be followed by a measured,
  explained tightening.

- Teach the fixture contract/integration harness to obtain this metric from the
  production public JSONL projection and `CausalReport`, filtering product kind
  `callable_construction` and summing its `settlements`.
- Use the same `fz2 interp` lens measured above. Do not silently substitute an
  in-process compile with a different root/session shape; if the harness lens
  must change, first re-measure it repeatedly and document the new baseline and
  reason.
- Declare the 2,299 ceiling in
  `fixtures2/behavior/enum_predicate_search.fz`, next to the timeout metadata.
- Keep both 20-second timeout overrides and their hang-backstop explanation.
- Update the fixture commentary and performance/fixture-metadata documentation
  so they describe the live detector rather than referring to this ticket as
  future work.
- Do not add a side table, a wall-clock assertion, or a test-only compiler
  counter. Do not add ceilings to unrelated fixtures.

## Tests

- Metadata parsing accepts the new maximum-metric declaration and rejects
  duplicate, malformed, or unsupported forms.
- The ceiling comparison has a red proof: a measured count above the declared
  maximum fails and reports fixture, metric, expected maximum, and actual count.
- `enum_predicate_search` passes at 2,299 on HEAD using emitted public telemetry.
- The test proves the signal is present/non-empty so a missing telemetry event
  cannot look like zero work.
- Existing public-trace causality, analysis-work, executable-inventory, full lib,
  and fixture-matrix tests remain green.

## Cleanup

Remove the stale 2,625/242 assumptions and the fixture's future-tense
`fz-f98.23` reference. Add no temporary counter or side-table entry that needs
later removal.

comments.text:
SCOPE NOTE, because a commit already carries this ticket's name.

`fz-f98.23: retire a wall-clock tripwire that was always red on CI` (main
120c86192, PR #102) landed only the RETIREMENT half -- the caps moved to 20s and
the fixture header now says plainly that they are hang backstops, deliberately
too loose to notice a perf regression.

This ticket's actual subject, the REPLACEMENT, is not done. None of its Checks
are met:

    enum_predicate_search carries a work ceiling                NOT MET
    the ceiling is derived from emitted telemetry               NOT MET
    the wall-clock overrides stay loose and documented          holds

So there is currently NO perf detector on that fixture at all. That is the gap
this ticket closes, and `git log` should not be read as closure.

title: enum_predicate_search still lacks a pull-work regression gate: cap callable-construction settlements at the current 2299 baseline
